resources.string: Send files, links and text instantly between your phone, tablet and computer.
Everything travels encrypted, directly between devices you trust. No account, no cloud, no tracking.
This is how your other devices will see it.
Relay will show your other devices here automatically. Open Relay on them and keep them on the same Wi-Fi.

1. Install Relay on your other device.
2. Connect both to the same Wi-Fi.
3. Open Relay on both. They find each other within a few seconds.

A few steps, once. After that they find each other by themselves.
Get Relay on your other devices
This app on the phone, and Relay for desktop on the computer from GitHub. On Windows, unzip it and run Relay.
Put the phone and the computer on the same network. If Windows asks about the firewall, choose Allow on private networks.
The computer appears on this phone under New nearby. Tap it, check that both screens show the same three shapes, and choose Trust on the computer.
Copy on one, paste on the other. Share to the computer from any app. On the computer, drag a file to the drop shelf on the left edge of the screen and drop it on this phone.
Both need the app from Google Play. Either phone can start the connection.
Join both phones to the same Wi-Fi. No Wi-Fi around? Turn on one phone’s hotspot and connect the other to it; no internet needed.
On either phone, tap the other under New nearby. Check that both screens show the same three shapes, then tap Trust on the second phone.
Share photos and files to the other phone from any app. Hold the two phones back to back to swap contact cards.
Install Relay for desktop on both
Download it from GitHub for Windows or Linux and run it on each computer. It sits in the system tray.
Both computers on the same Wi-Fi or the same wired network. Allow Relay through the firewall on private networks.
On one computer, click the other under New nearby. Check that both screens show the same three shapes, then choose Trust on the second computer.
Copy on one computer and paste on the other, or drag files onto the drop shelf at the left edge of the screen.
Every device you want to use needs Relay.
Android phones and tablets: this app
Windows, Linux and Mac: Relay for desktop
iPhone and iPad: Relay for iOS (in the works)
Anything else: open Relay Web in a browser
Your home Wi-Fi, or your phone’s hotspot. No internet needed: Relay talks directly between devices.
Tap the device and check the shapes
It appears under New nearby. Tap it, make sure both screens show the same three shapes, and tap Trust on the other device. You only do this once.

Your trusted devices work as one. Nothing asks you to accept: share to your computer, or drag a file onto the drop shelf at the left edge of your computer’s screen and drop it on this phone. It arrives ready to paste.
Text, photos and files you copy on your computer are ready to paste on this phone. Turn on Instant clipboard in Settings and what you copy here is ready on your computer too, without opening Relay.
Add the Send clipboard tile to Quick Settings, or use the button in Relay’s notification, to send what you just copied in another app.
In any app, tap Share and pick your computer. Relay sends it without opening.

Make sure Relay is open on it and both are on the same Wi-Fi, not a guest network. Office, school and hotel networks often keep devices apart; use your phone’s hotspot instead. Turning off a VPN can also help.
My Windows PC can’t see this phone

The first time Relay runs, Windows asks whether to allow it on your network. Choose Allow on private networks. If you missed it, open Windows Security, Firewall, Allow an app through the firewall, and tick Relay.
It stops working after a while
Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery. In Relay’s Settings, tap Allow under Keep Relay reachable. On Xiaomi phones, also turn on Autostart for Relay in the phone’s settings.
Relay for iPhone and iPad is in the works. Apple does not let apps read the clipboard or stay connected in the background, so on iPhone Relay works while it is open and through the Share menu.
Can anyone else see my files?
No. Everything travels encrypted directly between your devices, and only devices you trusted can send you anything. There is no Relay server and no account.
No devices yet. Open Relay on your other device and connect them first.
Sends anonymous counts of things like "a transfer finished", never file names, text or who your devices are. Off by default.
Two things and Relay is ready
Android asks before an app may do these. Relay needs both to reach your devices while it is not on screen.
So you know what arrived, and which device sent it.
Without this, Android stops Relay after a while and your other devices cannot reach this phone.
